blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE for antineoplastic hazardous drugs
stem: A nurse is administering an antineoplastic hazardous drug. Which PPE approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent gown with a closed front and tight-fitting cuffs, adding task-specific protection when exposure risk warrants it.
options.B: Use ordinary examination gloves without a gown when a closed-system transfer device is present because engineering controls replace protective clothing.
options.C: Use a surgical mask and eye protection without chemotherapy gloves because room ventilation is the primary control for liquid-drug skin exposure.
options.D: Wear a nonabsorbent gown without gloves when handling a closed infusion system because dermal exposure is negligible after preparation is complete.

rationale: A is correct. Current NIOSH guidance states that during administration or compounding of antineoplastic drugs, workers should wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent gown with a closed front and tight-fitting cuffs. NIOSH also recommends supplementary engineering controls, which reduce rather than replace exposure-control measures. Additional eye, face, or respiratory protection is selected when the task presents splash, aerosol, or inhalation risk. B, C, and D omit required glove/gown protection or incorrectly treat engineering/ventilation controls as substitutes for PPE.
educational_objective: Use chemotherapy gloves and an appropriate protective gown during antineoplastic hazardous-drug administration, with additional task-specific protection when exposure risk warrants it.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (CDC/NIOSH); NCSBN
source_document_title: Chemical Hazards Risk Factors; Antineoplastic Agents; Hazardous Drug Exposures in Healthcare; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NIOSH chemical-hazards page Aug. 12, 2024; hazardous-drug resources updated March 3, 2026 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NIOSH Chemical Hazards lines 83-89: avoid skin contact; during administration/compounding wear chemotherapy gloves and a nonabsorbent gown with closed front and tight-fitting cuffs; use supplementary engineering controls. NIOSH Engineering Controls: PPE includes chemotherapy gloves, protective gowns, eye/face protection, and respiratory protection when controls are inadequate for inhalation risk.
source_claim_supported: Current NIOSH guidance directly supports chemotherapy gloves plus nonabsorbent gown during antineoplastic administration and treats engineering controls as supplementary rather than a replacement for PPE.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: follow procedures for hazardous materials and promote staff/workplace safety.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; occupational-exposure claims rely on current NIOSH HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; matches NIOSH glove/gown and task-specific exposure-control guidance.
option_audit.B: Plausible engineering-control misconception but closed systems supplement rather than replace PPE.
option_audit.C: Plausible respiratory/splash framing but omits required dermal protection.
option_audit.D: Plausible closed-system shortcut but omits chemotherapy gloves during administration.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Options are similar in detail and structure; the key is not uniquely signaled.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor depends on simplistic always/never/only wording.
